en: present given in return; thank you gift

examples.ko: 결혼식에 와 주신 분들께 답례품을 드렸어요.
examples.en: We gave thank-you gifts to the people who came to the wedding.
I prepared small towels as return gifts for the first birthday party.

examples.ko: 답례품은 받는 분이 부담 없게 고르는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to pick a return gift that doesn't burden the recipient.

examples.ko: 선물을 받고 감사의 뜻으로 답례품을 보냈어요.
examples.en: After receiving a gift, I sent a gift back as thanks.

examples.ko: 손님들에게 줄 답례품 포장을 하느라 바빴어요.
examples.en: I was busy wrapping the return gifts for the guests.

examples.ko: 답례품이 너무 비싸면 오히려 부담스러울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the return gift is too expensive, it can actually feel burdensome.

explain: 결혼식, 돌잔치, 개업식 등에 와 준 사람이나 선물을 준 사람에게 감사의 뜻으로 주는 물건이에요. '답례'만 쓰면 인사나 보답하는 행동을 말하고, '답례품'은 그때 주는 물건을 가리켜요. 그냥 '선물'보다 보답이라는 느낌이 분명해요.

phrases.example: 돌잔치에 올 손님들을 위해 답례품을 준비했어요.
phrases.en: I prepared return gifts for the guests coming to the first-birthday party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사 전에 미리 마련할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when getting the gifts ready before an event.

phrases.en: We gave a thank-you gift to the people who came.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주다'의 높임말 '드리다'를 써서 손님께 공손하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Deurida' is the honorific of 'give', used politely toward guests.

phrases.en: I sent cookies as wedding return gifts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 행사의 답례품인지 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: You put the event name before it to say which occasion it is for.

explain_en: It is a gift given as thanks to people who came to an event such as a wedding, first-birthday party or shop opening, or who gave you a present. '답례' alone refers to the act of returning thanks, while '답례품' is the item itself. It carries a clearer sense of repayment than a plain '선물'.

examples.en: I test-drove a new car over the weekend.
You can test-drive an electric car at the showroom.

examples.ko: 직접 시승하면 승차감을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you test-drive it yourself, you can feel how it rides.

examples.ko: 시승하지 않고 차를 사는 건 불안해요.
examples.en: Buying a car without test-driving it makes me uneasy.
I keep thinking about the car I test-drove yesterday.
Reporters test-drove the new model first.

explain: '차를 시승하다'처럼 '을/를'과 함께 써요. 자주 '시승해 보다'의 꼴로 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '타 보다'라고 하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 차를 사기 전에 꼭 시승해 보세요.
phrases.en: Be sure to test-drive the car before buying it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시승하다'를 가장 자주 쓰는 꼴로, 직접 경험해 본다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form of 시승하다, with the feel of trying it out yourself.

phrases.example: 이 매장에서는 신형 모델을 시승할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can test-drive the new model at this dealership.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시승이 가능한지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say whether a test drive is possible.

phrases.example: 새 차를 한번 타 보고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to try riding in the new car.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시승하다'보다 편한 일상 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual everyday expression than 시승하다.

explain_en: It takes an object with '을/를', as in '차를 시승하다'. It often appears as '시승해 보다'. In everyday talk people also just say '타 보다'.

examples.en: How much is the gym's joining fee?
To join the club, you have to pay a joining fee.

examples.ko: 입회비는 처음에 한 번만 내면 돼요.
examples.en: You only have to pay the joining fee once at the beginning.

examples.ko: 입회비 삼만 원과 월회비 만 원을 냈어요.
examples.en: I paid a 30,000 won joining fee and a 10,000 won monthly fee.
There's an event where they discount the joining fee.
I paid the joining fee and got my membership card too.

explain: 모임이나 동호회, 운동 시설에 처음 들어갈 때 한 번 내는 돈이에요. 매달 내는 '월회비', 매년 내는 '연회비'와 구별해서 쓰고, '가입비'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I paid the entrance fee to join the club.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임에 처음 들어갈 때 돈을 내는 상황에서 가장 흔히 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for paying money when first joining a group.

phrases.example: 이번 달에는 입회비 면제 행사를 해요.
phrases.en: This month there's an entrance fee waiver promotion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 헬스장이나 모임 광고에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in ads for gyms and clubs.

phrases.en: How much is the membership fee?
phrases.nuance_ko: 입회비와 비슷한 뜻이고 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning to 입회비, and an easier word in everyday conversation.

explain_en: It is the one-time money you pay when first joining a club, group or gym. Do not confuse it with 월회비 (monthly fee) or 연회비 (annual fee), and people also say 가입비.

en: to appear; to contribute funds; to perform

examples.en: That actor appears in a new drama.
I appeared on a TV program yesterday.
It is a show where singers all perform together.

examples.ko: 그 배우가 주인공으로 출연한 영화가 큰 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: The film in which that actor starred as the lead became very popular.

examples.ko: 그 가수가 내년에 영화에 출연할 거라는 소식이 있어요.
examples.en: There is news that the singer will appear in a film next year.
My child said they want to appear in a commercial.

explain: 방송·영화·공연에 나오는 것을 말하고, 배우뿐 아니라 가수나 손님으로 나오는 사람에게도 써요. 보통 '~에 출연하다' 형태예요. 일상 대화에서는 '나오다'도 많이 써서 '그 드라마에 나와요'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: That singer appears in a movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '출연하다' 앞에 '~에'를 붙여 어디에 나오는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 에 before the verb to say which show or film someone appears in.

phrases.example: 다음 달에 그 프로그램에 출연할 거예요.
phrases.en: I will appear on that program next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 나올 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a future appearance.

phrases.en: Our neighborhood was on TV.
phrases.nuance_ko: '출연하다'보다 쉬운 일상 표현이고, 사람뿐 아니라 장소에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler everyday phrase that also works for places, not only people.

explain_en: Perform in a drama or program; also contribute money. It covers appearing in a broadcast, film, or stage show, and applies to singers and guests as well as actors. It normally takes the form '~에 출연하다'. In casual talk, '나오다' is also common, as in '그 드라마에 나와요'.

t90.ax: That actor appears in a new drama.

examples.ko: 메일을 보낸 지 사흘이 지났는데 아직 회신이 없어요.
examples.en: It's been three days since I sent the email and there's no reply yet.
I'll be waiting for your answer.
Please send a reply by Friday at the latest.
I was glad to get a quick reply from the customer.

examples.ko: 회신 주소가 달라서 메일이 전달되지 않았어요.
examples.en: The reply address was different, so the email wasn't delivered.

examples.ko: 면접 결과는 이메일 회신으로 알려 드릴게요.
examples.en: We'll let you know the interview result by email reply.

explain: 메일 끝에 쓰는 '회신 부탁드립니다'처럼 회사에서 아주 자주 써요. 친구끼리는 '답장'이나 '답'이라고 해요. '회신을 주다', '회신을 받다', '회신을 기다리다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Please check and give me a reply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 메일이나 업무에서 답을 달라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in emails or work when asking for an answer.

phrases.en: I haven't received a reply yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 답을 받았는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say whether you got an answer.

phrases.en: I got a reply from my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '회신'보다 편해서 친구 사이나 일상에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More casual than 'hoesin', used among friends and daily life.

explain_en: Formal reply to an inquiry or official mail, business use. It is very common in work email, as in 회신 부탁드립니다. Friends say 답장 or 답 instead. Typical patterns are 회신을 주다, 회신을 받다, 회신을 기다리다.

t90.ax: I'll be waiting for your answer.

en: to suggest; to propose; to recommend

examples.ko: 학생들이 학교에 급식 시간을 늘려 달라고 건의했어요.
examples.en: The students requested that the school lengthen lunch time.
May I put forward a new idea at the meeting?
The employees proposed to the boss that vacation be extended.
If something is inconvenient, you can submit your suggestion to the district office.
What we suggested will be applied from next month.
The class president went to the teachers' room to make a request.

explain: 윗사람이나 기관에 의견을 정식으로 말할 때 써요. '제안하다'는 동료에게도 쓰지만 '건의하다'는 보통 아래에서 위로 말해요. '건의 사항', '건의함'도 같이 알아 두세요.

phrases.example: 건의 사항이 있으면 이 상자에 넣어 주세요.
phrases.en: If you have suggestions, please put them in this box.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건의하는 내용을 가리키는 명사 표현이에요. 학교나 회사에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun expression for what is being suggested, often used at schools and companies.

phrases.en: There is a suggestion box at the front of the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의견을 넣는 상자예요. 건의를 모으는 장소를 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A box where opinions are put, meaning a place to collect suggestions.

phrases.example: 선생님께 숙제를 줄여 달라고 건의해 볼게요.
phrases.en: I'll try suggesting to the teacher that they reduce the homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보다'가 붙어 조심스럽게 시도해 본다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 보다' gives a feeling of carefully giving it a try.

explain_en: Suggest an improvement to a boss, teacher or authority. Used when formally putting an opinion to a superior or an institution. '제안하다' can be used with peers, but '건의하다' usually goes from lower to higher. Also learn '건의 사항' (suggestions) and '건의함' (suggestion box).

t90.ax: May I put forward a new idea at the meeting?

examples.en: When I moved, I called a cleaning service company.

examples.ko: 대행업체에 맡기면 서류 준비가 훨씬 편해요.
examples.en: If you leave it to an agency, preparing the documents is much easier.
This agency's fee isn't expensive.
We signed a new contract with an advertising agency.

examples.ko: 대행업체가 일을 늦게 끝내서 약속이 밀렸어요.
examples.en: The agency finished the work late, so our appointment was pushed back.

examples.ko: 믿을 만한 대행업체를 찾으려고 후기를 읽고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm reading reviews to find a trustworthy agency.

explain: '청소 대행', '광고 대행', '이사 대행'처럼 앞에 대신 해 주는 일의 이름이 붙어요. '대행사'도 비슷하게 쓰는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '대신 해 주는 회사'라고 풀어 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I asked an agency to prepare the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대행업체'보다 짧고 자주 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter, very common word with a similar meaning.

phrases.example: 광고 대행업체에서 일한 지 삼 년 됐어요.
phrases.en: I've worked at an advertising agency for three years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 일의 이름을 붙여 어떤 일을 대신 해 주는지 밝혀요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the name of the job before it to say what the agency does.

phrases.en: I'm busy, so I decided to use an agency.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 하지 않고 서비스를 쓴다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you use a service instead of doing the task yourself.

explain_en: The name of the job being done on your behalf goes in front, as in '청소 대행', '광고 대행' or '이사 대행'. '대행사' is used in a similar way. In daily talk people also just say '대신 해 주는 회사' (a company that does it for you).

en: to distribute widely; to release; to circulate

examples.en: The school handed out notices to the students.
The company releases the new app for free.

examples.ko: 파일을 배포하기 전에 한 번 더 확인하세요.
examples.en: Check once more before you release the file.
City Hall will hand out maps to citizens.
You must not distribute these materials.

examples.ko: 우리가 만든 프로그램을 인터넷에 배포하고 있어요.
examples.en: We are releasing the program we made on the internet.

explain: '나눠 주다'보다 딱딱한 말이에요. 종이를 손으로 줄 때는 '나눠 주다'가 일상적이고, 자료나 프로그램을 많은 사람에게 내놓을 때는 배포하다를 써요. IT 쪽에서는 소프트웨어를 내놓는 일도 배포라고 해요.

phrases.en: The library distributes guide booklets for free.
phrases.nuance_ko: 값을 받지 않고 많은 사람에게 내놓는다는 뜻으로 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing meaning to give something out to many people at no charge.

phrases.en: The teacher hands out paper to the students.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배포하다'보다 쉽고 일상적인 말이라서 손으로 직접 줄 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, everyday word that suits handing things out directly.

phrases.example: 회사는 다음 달에 새 버전을 배포할 계획이에요.
phrases.en: The company plans to release a new version next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 내놓을 계획을 말할 때 쓰는 공식적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression for stating a plan to release something.

explain_en: Active, someone gives out leaflets, notices or software to many people. It is stiffer than '나눠 주다'. For paper handed out by hand, '나눠 주다' is the everyday choice, while 배포하다 fits materials or programs offered to many people. In IT, releasing software is also called 배포.

examples.en: A photo was attached to the email.
Please open the attached file.
The document was not attached, so I sent it again.

examples.ko: 첨부되는 파일은 크기가 10MB를 넘으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Attached files must not be larger than 10 MB.
An instruction sheet will be attached to the contract too.
The picture that came attached will not open.

explain: 메일과 서류에서 자주 보는 말이에요. 파일을 붙이는 사람은 '첨부하다', 붙어 있는 파일을 말할 때는 '첨부되다'나 '첨부된 파일'을 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '붙이다', '같이 보내다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Please check the attached file.
phrases.nuance_ko: 메일에 붙어 있는 파일을 가리키는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to refer to a file attached to an email.

phrases.en: I attached the documents to the email.
phrases.nuance_ko: 파일을 붙이는 사람이 쓰는 말이에요. 붙어 있는 상태는 '첨부되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used by the person who attaches the file; for the state of being attached, use '첨부되다'.

phrases.en: The file was not attached.
phrases.nuance_ko: 메일을 받았는데 파일이 없을 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when you got an email but the file is missing.

explain_en: You see it often in emails and paperwork. The person who adds a file '첨부하다', and the file that is already there is '첨부되다' or '첨부된 파일'. In casual talk people say '붙이다' or '같이 보내다'.

en: to correct; to edit; to mark up

examples.ko: 영어 에세이 첨삭을 받고 나서 문장이 많이 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: After getting my English essay corrected, my sentences got a lot better.

examples.ko: 첨삭 결과에는 틀린 이유까지 적혀 있어서 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: The correction results even say why things were wrong, so they help.
My teacher corrected my self-introduction for me.
I looked for mistakes while editing the writing myself.
I asked my friend to correct it for me.

examples.ko: 첨삭한 글을 다시 읽고 고쳐 썼어요.
examples.en: I reread the corrected piece and rewrote it.

explain: 주로 작문, 자기소개서, 보고서처럼 글을 선생님이나 전문가가 고쳐 주는 일에 써요. '첨삭을 받다', '첨삭해 주다' 형태로 자주 나오고, 그냥 '고치다'보다 설명과 조언이 같이 있는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I got my self-introduction corrected by my teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글을 고쳐 주는 도움을 받는 입장에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person receiving the correction.

phrases.en: Please correct and comment on this writing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글을 고쳐 달라고 공손하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request for someone to edit your writing.

phrases.en: My teacher carefully corrects my writing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글을 목적어로 하는 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic usage with writing as the object.
phrases.en_equiv: to edit a piece of writing

explain_en: Teacher or editor adds and deletes in a student's writing. It is mainly used when a teacher or expert fixes writing such as essays, self-introductions and reports. It often appears as '첨삭을 받다' or '첨삭해 주다', and feels like more than a plain '고치다' because explanations and advice usually come with it.

t90.ax: I asked my friend to correct it for me.

examples.en: The school is bringing in a famous professor.
The university invited a teacher from abroad.
We will bring in a lecturer next semester.
I went to an event where an expert was invited to speak.
The church is looking to bring in a new pastor.

examples.ko: 회사가 디자이너를 초빙해서 새 제품을 만들었어요.
examples.en: The company brought in a designer and made a new product.

explain: '초빙하다'는 전문가나 선생님을 모셔 올 때 써요. 파티나 식사에 친구를 부를 때는 '초대하다'를 써야 자연스러워요. 친구에게 '초빙하다'라고 하면 어색해요.

phrases.en: He was invited to the university as a professor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 초빙을 받는 쪽을 주어로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Passive form with the invited person as the subject.

phrases.en: We invite a lecturer and hold a special class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모셔 온 다음에 할 일을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Connective form for what happens after inviting someone.

phrases.en: The guest lecturer's class is fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외부에서 모셔 온 강사를 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a lecturer brought in from outside.

explain_en: Formal: bring in a famous or skilled person for a lecture. 초빙하다 is for bringing in an expert or a teacher. To invite a friend to a party or a meal, 초대하다 is the natural word, and 초빙하다 would sound odd.

t90.ax: We will bring in a lecturer next semester.

examples.ko: 필기도구를 안 가져와서 친구에게 펜을 빌렸어요.
examples.en: I didn't bring writing supplies, so I borrowed a pen from my friend.
Bring only writing supplies to the exam room.
I had nothing to write with, so I took notes on my phone.
I put writing supplies and a notebook in my school bag.
I finished preparing my writing supplies last night.
Among writing instruments, a ballpoint pen is the most convenient.

explain: 연필, 볼펜, 샤프처럼 글씨를 쓰는 물건을 묶어 부르는 말이에요. '문구'는 가위, 풀, 공책까지 더 넓게 가리켜요. 시험 안내문에 '필기도구 지참'이라고 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Please be sure to bring writing instruments to the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필기도구와 같은 뜻이지만 더 짧고 글에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as the headword, but shorter and more common in writing.

phrases.en: I pack my writing supplies before class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가방에 필요한 물건을 준비해 넣는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to get your supplies ready and put them in your bag.

phrases.en: I had no pen, so I borrowed writing supplies from a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깜빡하고 안 가져왔을 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when you forgot to bring your own.

explain_en: It groups together things you write with, such as pencils, ballpoint pens and mechanical pencils. '문구' is broader and also includes scissors, glue and notebooks. Exam notices often say '필기도구 지참' (bring writing supplies).

en: to cooperate; to collaborate; to coordinate

examples.en: Please cooperate actively with the survey.
The neighbors agreed to cooperate with the construction.

examples.ko: 협조하지 않으면 일이 늦어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If people don't cooperate, work can be delayed.
The guests cooperated, so the event ended well.

examples.ko: 잘 협조하는 사람 덕분에 일이 빨라요.
examples.en: Thanks to people who cooperate well, the work is fast.

examples.ko: 서로 협조할 때 팀이 더 잘 돌아가요.
examples.en: A team runs better when members cooperate with each other.

explain: '도와주다'는 누구에게나 쓰는 쉬운 말이고, '협조하다'는 회사, 공공기관, 행사처럼 공식적인 일에서 부탁하거나 요청할 때 써요. 안내문에서는 '협조 부탁드립니다'라는 말을 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Parking work is under way, so we ask for your cooperation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 공식적인 자리에서 정중하게 부탁하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request used in notices and formal situations.

phrases.en: I asked the neighbors for their cooperation with the construction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도움을 정식으로 요청한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means formally requesting help.

phrases.en: A neighbor helped with my move.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누구에게나 쓸 수 있는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy word that can be used with anyone.

explain_en: Help or go along with someone's request, often at work. '도와주다' is the easy everyday word for helping anyone, while '협조하다' is for formal situations like companies, public offices, and events where you ask for cooperation. Notices often say '협조 부탁드립니다'.

dis.h: help or comply with someone's request
gh: general, neutral: work together toward a goal
official joint action, police or governments

p.n: 협조 means going along with or assisting a request; 협력 sounds like equal partners.

t90.ax: Please cooperate actively with the survey.

en: to reply; to answer; to write back

examples.en: I reply to emails I receive as soon as I can.
I replied to the person in charge yesterday afternoon.
I will reply by tomorrow.
I'll check what you asked and get back to you.
I was busy and couldn't reply.

examples.ko: 회신하시기 전에 첨부 파일을 먼저 확인해 주세요.
examples.en: Please check the attachment before you reply.

explain: '답장하다'보다 딱딱해서 회사 메일이나 공문에 써요. '회신 주세요'처럼 '하다' 없이 쓰는 말도 아주 많이 들려요. 격식 있는 자리에서는 '회신해 드리겠습니다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: Please reply by tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다' 없이 쓰는 말로 업무 메일에서 아주 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used without 'hada' and very common in work emails.

phrases.en: I saw the message and replied right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: '회신하다'보다 부드러워서 일상에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than 'hoesinhada' and used in daily life.

phrases.en: I'll reply to you right after I check.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대를 높이는 격식 있는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal, respectful way to say it to someone.

explain_en: Formal written reply to an inquiry, email, or official message. It is stiffer than 답장하다 and fits work email and official documents. Phrases like 회신 주세요 without 하다 are also very common. In formal settings you say 회신해 드리겠습니다.
